specs.v: Room temperature, not in the fridge

description.html: Superworms are beetle larvae, larger than mealworms, and lizards love them for their lively movement. They are nutritious and filling, but they have more fat and a tougher outer skin than dubia roaches, so use them as an addition and for variety rather than as the only food. They suit bearded dragons, leopard geckos, chameleons, tegus and other insect eaters.

description.text: Sizes and which animals they suit

description.html: They come in three sizes: small for younger animals, medium for juveniles and large for adult lizards. Size rule: the insect should not be wider than the space between the animal's eyes. Superworms have strong jaws, so do not give them to very small babies and do not leave uneaten ones in the terrarium.

Unlike mealworms, do not keep superworms in the fridge, because they do not tolerate cold. Keep them at room temperature in a box with a little bran or rolled oats and a piece of vegetable. Dust them with calcium before feeding. Read more about combining live foods on our lizard food page.
